media.narrative_summary: This is a Japanese-language social media video from the account 'Rei Lab | 若返り美容研究室' posted August 29, 2026. Set to gentle acoustic guitar music, the video uses AI-generated imagery of two Shiba Inu dogs in lab coats to deliver a wellness message. The opening frames claim that three commonly perceived 'healthy' foods actually accelerate aging: excess fruit leads to blood sugar spikes and yellowed skin, low-fat yogurt causes glycation, and acai bowls cause excessive antioxidant intake. The video then transitions to a 'save-worthy 5 replacements' list: swap excess fruit for insoluble dietary fiber, low-fat yogurt for unsweetened Greek yogurt, acai for a small amount of berries, morning fruit juice for vegetable soup, and sweet protein bars for nuts. On-screen text urges viewers to save the post and change their breakfast starting today, and to follow Rei Lab for more. The tone is educational, promotional for the brand's anti-aging research, and visually designed as a friendly, shareable infographic.

media.narrative_summary: The post is a five-slide carousel advertisement for 'Rei Lab – 若返り美容研究所' (Rejuvenation Research Lab), starring two cute anthropomorphic dogs—a white Shiba Inu and a black-and-tan Shiba Inu—both dressed in white scientist lab coats. The visual style is soft, warm, photorealistic 3D illustration set in a bright laboratory with beakers, test tubes, plants, and skincare bottles labeled '肌' (skin), '腸' (gut), and '睡眠' (sleep). Slide 1 introduces the lab's mission: 'Rei Lab | 若返り研究室がめざす1つの答え。' (The one answer Rei Lab aims for) with the tagline '美容は、全部つながっている' (Beauty is all connected). Slide 2 states the MISSION to prove beauty is connected throughout the whole body, not just the skin surface. Slide 3 illustrates the five interconnected research areas around Rei Lab: 肌 (skin), 睡眠 (sleep), 生活習慣 (lifestyle habits), 食事 (diet), and 腸 (gut). Slide 4 is a call to action: '一緒に、研究する。保存して、まずは1週間試す。フォローで続きを。' (Research together. Save it and try for one week first. Follow for the continuation.) with a teaser for next time on sleep and aging appearance. The final slides show the dogs conducting experiments with pipettes and clipboards. The accompanying Japanese caption shares a personal story of spending 1 million yen on serums in one's 30s, monthly disappointment, and a lab teacher saying 'You're not bad, it just wasn't only about the skin,' asking followers to share similar experiences and to save and share. The tone is gentle, scientific, and empathetic, positioning beauty as holistic science rather than quick-fix cosmetics.
